Definition: from G4862 and G3076; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone:--be grieved.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus looks round on the Pharisees in the synagogue with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, and then tells the man with the withered hand to stretch it out. His grief and His anger stand together: He is sorrowful over hearts that will not soften, and He heals anyway.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that a hard heart grieves Jesus more than it provokes Him, and I hold that the same grief should move me to pray for hard hearts rather than merely condemn them.
